dēngshān — "to climb a mountain".
zhōumò wǒmen zuò huǒchē qù dēngshān — At the weekend we're taking the train to go climbing.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.
dēngshān is built from dēng 'to ascend' and 山 'a mountain', both inherited from Middle Chinese, tong and srean (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to rise' and 'to go up'.
One more word for getting around.

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for an account of a journey, then the Mandarin for to climb a mountain.
shāndǐng — "top of a mountain; summit".
cóng zhèr wǎng qián zǒu shí fēnzhōng jiù dào shāndǐng le — Walk on for ten minutes from here and you'll be at the top.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.
shāndǐng is built from 山 'a mountain' and dǐng 'the top', both inherited from Middle Chinese, srean and tengX (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the second as the crown of the head.
One more word for getting around.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 日出

segments.text: 日出 — rìchū — "sunrise".
我们早上五点起来看日出 wǒmen zǎoshang wǔ diǎn qǐlai kàn rìchū — We're getting up at five in the morning to watch the sunrise.
日出 (rìchū) is built from 日 'the sun' and 出 'to come out', both inherited from Middle Chinese, nyit and tsyhwit (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription).
One more word for getting around.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 下山

segments.text: 下山 — xiàshān — "to come down a mountain".
下山以后我们坐车回酒店 xiàshān yǐhòu wǒmen zuò chē huí jiǔdiàn — After coming down the mountain, we take the bus back to the hotel.

下山 (xiàshān) is built from 下 'to go down' and 山 'a mountain', both inherited from Middle Chinese, haeX and srean (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'low' and 'to come down'.
One more word for getting around.
